**MAGNESIUM**  
It is an intracellular ion and a cofactor for hundreds of enzymes involved in regulating the effects of insulin . Due to its mechanisms of regulating glycemic and neurological functions, magnesium is associated with insulin resistance and depression, including polycystic ovary syndrome, as well as some cardiovascular diseases and diabetes. A systematic review found that high magnesium levels were associated with a general decrease in insulin resistance (IR), based on four epidemiological studies in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, when analyzing the results of three randomized clinical trials (RCTs), the effects of magnesium supplementation on IR in these women were variable.
